propositions: When two bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git ls-remote returns the ref at two SHAs and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable and git-remote-s3's push path unable to converge due to ambiguous ref resolution.

git-remote-s3's upstream Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocks on input() on EOF) and discards the non-chosen head's events entirely rather than merging them, causing unacceptable data loss in rebar's append-only event log where divergent heads carry unique ticket events.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref S3 lock (IfNoneMatch/60s TTL), re-enumerate bundles under lock (TOCTOU guard), fetch all head commits locally, fold them via iterated 2-parent merges (following sync's existing lossless semantics), write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting originals (crash-safe ordering), and release the lock; all S3 access routes through git_remote_s3's own S3Remote and boto3 client, adding no hard dependency to core rebar.
On genuine non-derived-file merge conflict the doctor must abort without deleting any remote bundles, release both locks, and surface the fsck-recover hint rather than silently discarding a parent.

Concurrent doctor processes must serialize via the helper's S3 lock such that exactly one performs the merge while others observe lock contention and back off, converging on the winner's single healed bundle rather than thrashing on self-heals.

The heal is invoked from push_tickets_branch's non-FF retry path (gated by healed_once to prevent thrash), detected by _is_multi_bundle matching the 'multiple bundles exists on server' and 'multiple updates for ref' stderr signatures, then the push retries against the now-single merged bundle.
